priorFindingsResolution.status: NOT RESOLVED (code-level claim is false; risk is masked operationally, not fixed in code)
priorFindingsResolution.note: Re-examined healthcheck-lib.sh:33-39. The builder's claim ('mkdir atomic + lost-steal returns 0') is true ONLY for the single initial `mkdir` on line 34 -- that part was already correct before round 3. The steal path itself (lines 35-38: `rmdir "$LOCK_DIR" ... ; mkdir "$LOCK_DIR" ... || return 0`) is NOT an atomic compound operation across two processes: if two invocations A and B both observe the lock as stale (age>=10min) at nearly the same time, A's rmdir+mkdir can succeed, and then B's rmdir (which does not check who owns the directory) unconditionally deletes A's freshly-created lock, after which B's own mkdir also succeeds. Both A and B then pass the `|| return 0` guard and BOTH execute hc_run's body concurrently -- the exact double-run this fix was supposed to close. The `return 0`-for-the-loser guarantee the builder cites literally cannot fire in this interleaving, because B's mkdir does not fail. The practical exploit window is reduced by launchd's default one-running-instance-per-Label scheduling plus ThrottleInterval=60 on the plist (capafy-loop/launchd/ai.anicca.capafy-loop-healthcheck.plist:6), which is an OPERATIONAL mitigation, not a code fix, and does not protect against a manual/ad-hoc re-invocation of the same healthcheck script or a launchd sleep/wake catch-up double-fire. Verdict: the specific safety property asked about (loser always gets return 0) is FALSE as written.

Confirmed: hc_is_stuck_pane() is defined once in healthcheck-lib.sh:16-20, and test-healthcheck-lib.sh:6 sources healthcheck-lib.sh directly (`source ".../healthcheck-lib.sh"`) and calls the real hc_is_stuck_pane function (test-healthcheck-lib.sh:7) with no local re-implementation. No duplication remains; the test exercises the production predicate, not a copy. All 6 test cases (idle picker->FIRE, active-generation-with-esc-to-interrupt->OK, healthy-idle->OK, free-text-await->FIRE, confirm-dialog->FIRE, active-searching-with-esc-to-interrupt->OK) were re-traced by hand against the current predicate and all 6 are still predicted to pass.

The literal bug (LM_NOTE interpolating the file path instead of the hours) is fixed: verify-loops-audit.sh:26-28 now computes LMH via stale_hrs() (a real integer hour count) and LM_MRR via a grep+awk of the loop's own STATE.md, and LM_NOTE:28 interpolates `${LMH}h` and `$LM_MRR` correctly -- confirmed by direct read, not just the inline comment. Additionally confirmed (going one level deeper than the round-3 review did) that life-manager-loop/loop.sh:24-39 computes LM_MRR via a genuinely independent, deterministic curl to the live Stripe Subscriptions API (not an LLM self-report), so the value the audit surfaces is grounded in real Stripe data on every daily LM pass, not a self-graded marker. Residual (non-blocking) caveat: the audit itself does not re-curl Stripe at audit time -- it only displays whatever loop.sh last wrote -- so if the daily LM cron silently stopped running loop.sh's STEP1 while still touching the heartbeat, MRR would go stale without necessarily tripping LMH; this was not observed on disk (STATE.md:3 last_wake_utc is consistent with the last-pass heartbeat) and is not being raised as a new finding since it is inherent to a once-daily-cadence measurement, not a defect in this fix.

priorFindingsResolution.status: PARTIALLY RESOLVED -- downgraded severity, not closed
priorFindingsResolution.note: Confirmed self-fix.sh:16 sets MAX_FIXER_MIN=180 (was 45). This closes the specific critical failure mode from round 3 (45min was clearly shorter than a normal fix). However the underlying design flaw is unchanged: the hung-fixer determination (self-fix.sh:22-29) is PURELY a wall-clock age check against STARTMARK, with no reuse of the pane-liveness heuristic the codebase already has and uses elsewhere for exactly this purpose (hc_is_stuck_pane / 'esc to interrupt' detection in healthcheck-lib.sh:16-20,58-63). Any genuinely-still-working fixer (e.g. a slow browser-automation rebuild, a flaky CI loop) that legitimately runs longer than 180 minutes WILL be killed and respawned from scratch by the next self-fix.sh invocation, discarding all progress, on the code's own comment's unverified assumption that 'a real fix rarely needs >3h' (self-fix.sh:16-19). Severity reduced from critical to major because 180min is materially more realistic than 45min, but the finding is not resolved, only its acuteness reduced.

priorFindingsResolution.status: CONFIRMED STILL PRESENT, unchanged, builder correctly characterized as minor
priorFindingsResolution.note: self-fix.sh:28 (`tmux -S "$SOCK" kill-session ...; pkill -f "claude --name $SESSION" ...`) still only targets the tmux session and the specific named claude process; it does not enumerate or kill any grandchild processes (background browser automation, curl/python helpers) the fixer may have spawned with & or nohup during its run. Agreed this is minor in isolation, but it compounds with the still-open FIND-023 gap: every forced kill-respawn cycle of a legitimately-long-running fixer is one more orphan-leak opportunity, not zero as the 'minor, accepted' framing implies in isolation.

newFindingsThisRound.summary: self-fix.sh's loop-name argument is inconsistent across call sites: healthcheck-lib.sh's automated escalation uses the LONG form ('capafy-loop', 'reddit-loop', 'life-manager-loop'), while every other call site (the LLM's own STEP0/ACT-failure self-heal prompts, verify-loops-audit.sh's independent stale-output escalation, and verify-loops.sh's own result-marker display) uses the SHORT form ('capafy', 'reddit', 'life-manager'). Since self-fix.sh derives both its tmux de-dup session name and its RESULT marker filename from this single un-normalized argument, this splits the SAME loop into two disjoint identities. CONFIRMED ON DISK, not theoretical: /Users/anicca/.openclaw/state/.self-fix-capafy-loop.result exists with a real SUCCESS record (commit e86bb98e, published skill, HTTP-200-verified logo URL, ledger 11->12), while .self-fix-capafy.result -- the filename verify-loops.sh actually reads -- does not exist. The system's own anti-fake verifier is already blind to a real, successful self-fix event. The same name split also means healthcheck-lib.sh's case-(d) output-stale escalation (HC_OUTPUT_STALE_HRS=30 for both capafy and reddit) and verify-loops-audit.sh's independent >=30h stale-output escalation for the SAME artifacts can spawn two mutually-unaware, full-power Opus dev sessions against the identical blocker with no coordination.

finalAssessment.summary: The system is NOT sound. Two genuinely new, disk-confirmed defects were found this round that were not present in the round-3 finding set: (1) FIND-020's fix is a false safety claim -- the lock-steal path is still a TOCTOU race at the code level, only masked by launchd scheduling behavior, not eliminated; (2) FIND-025, a critical, disk-CONFIRMED (not merely traced) loop-name inconsistency that (a) makes the system's own anti-fake verifier blind to at least one real, already-happened successful self-fix, and (b) creates a concrete path for two independent full-power Opus fixers to be spawned concurrently, unaware of each other, against the same blocker. FIND-023's fix genuinely reduces severity (45min->180min) but does not close the underlying design gap (no pane-liveness check reused for fixer-hung detection). No path was found where the system waits for un-sanctioned human input, and no fabricated/masked success was found for the loops' own STATE.md revenue reporting (that part is genuinely sound, backed by live Stripe/HTTP checks) -- but the self-heal layer's own internal bookkeeping is demonstrably inconsistent and, in the capafy case, already silently failing to report a real success to the intended verifier today.
